new_entities.name: Bifidobacterium infantis
new_entities.description: A probiotic strain studied for irritable bowel syndrome and related gastrointestinal symptoms.

new_entities.name: Diarrhea-predominant IBS symptoms
new_entities.description: Abdominal pain, bloating, urgency, loose stools, and related symptom burden in diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome.

edges.effect_quant: A 362-patient randomized trial found that B. infantis 35624 at 1 × 10^8 CFU was superior to placebo for abdominal pain and composite IBS symptoms, but later microbiota follow-up data did not show parallel symptom improvement and the strongest published clinical support is mostly IBS-wide rather than strictly IBS-D-specific.
edges.population: adults with irritable bowel syndrome, including mixed bowel-habit cohorts with potential applicability to diarrhea-predominant symptoms
edges.mechanism: B. infantis is thought to modify immune signaling and gut microbial interactions that contribute to pain, bloating, and bowel instability. In practice, however, the symptom benefit appears strain- and dose-specific and may not map neatly onto IBS-D alone.
edges.summary: Bifidobacterium infantis may improve diarrhea-predominant IBS symptoms, but the evidence is more convincing for broader IBS symptom reduction than for a pure IBS-D-specific effect. This is a plausible and relatively consumer-relevant probiotic signal, but not a settled one.
edges.caveats: Much of the best evidence comes from IBS cohorts that include multiple bowel-habit subtypes rather than only IBS-D patients. This edge should therefore stay modest and subtype-aware rather than claiming a highly specific anti-diarrheal effect.

evidence.citation: Whorwell PJ et al 2006 Am J Gastroenterol
evidence.notes: Efficacy of an encapsulated probiotic Bifidobacterium infantis 35624 in women with irritable bowel syndrome.

evidence.notes: Fecal excretion of Bifidobacterium infantis 35624 and changes in fecal microbiota after eight weeks of oral supplementation with encapsulated probiotic.
